key_insight: ShapeR enables reliable generation of complete 3D object shapes from casually captured, noisy image sequences by conditioning a generative model on sparse SLAM-derived geometry, multi-view crops, and semantic cues. It is robust to occlusion, incomplete segmentation, and real-world capture artifacts.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between lab-quality 3D reconstruction inputs and real-world casual captures by handling sparse, unsegmented, and occluded observations to produce accurate conditional 3D shapes.
method: Preprocess casual video: use off-the-shelf visual-inertial SLAM, 3D detectors, and vision–language models to extract per-object sparse SLAM points, multi-view image crops, poses, and semantic labels.
Feed these noisy, object-centric cues into a robust conditional 3D generative model that completes and refines full object geometry despite occlusions and segmentation errors.
Train and evaluate the system to prioritize resilience to realistic capture artifacts (sparsity, occlusions, viewpoint gaps) rather than relying on clean, segmented inputs.
impact: Makes conditional 3D shape generation practical for in-the-wild captures (mobile phones, robotics, AR) by reducing dependence on curated data and brittle preprocessing. Practitioners can integrate ShapeR-style pipelines to get reliable 3D assets from casual scans and noisy sensor streams.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing casual capture → SLAM + detectors + VLM → per-object sparse cues → conditional generative model → completed 3D shape
Before/after comparisons: sparse SLAM point cloud and multi-view crops next to the reconstructed 3D mesh or occupancy/grid output
Robustness plot: reconstruction quality (e.g., IoU or chamfer) vs. input sparsity/occlusion level
Icon set: camera/phone for casual capture, SLAM map icon, language/label icon, and a 3D mesh icon to communicate components at a glance
paper_title: ShapeR: Robust Conditional 3D Shape Generation from Casual Captures
paper_authors: Yawar Siddiqui, Duncan Frost, Samir Aroudj, Armen Avetisyan, Henry Howard-Jenkins
